comment: Cross-language golden vectors for the commissioned safety binding. A producer must emit these exact canonical bytes; an independent verifier in a different language must accept every case in 'cases' and refuse every case in 'reject_cases' with the declared reason, evaluated against the declared verifier_context. Signed with the TEST-ONLY seeds below - never use them in production. The commissioning and provisioning seeds are deliberately distinct: a corpus sharing one key could not express wrong_authority at all.
canonical_form: ori-specs/gateway-mqtt-canonical-json/v1.md, numbers additionally constrained to the D-011 agreement zone
signed_over: canonical bytes of the 'binding' object, not the envelope
authority_rule: binding.signing_key is compared against configured anchors as raw key material before the signature is verified; signer_id is an audit label and is never an authority input
firmware_profile_comment: The mapping a firmware device may act on. Signed by the commissioning authority and bound to the binding hash, because a manifest reference proves only that firmware claims a relationship to a binding - a build system can embed a correct hash beside a wrong mapping.
envelope_comment: The wire wrapper around a signed document. Closed like everything else: signature encoding and decoded length are grammar, and an unknown field beside the signature is outside the signed bytes and therefore unauthenticated by construction.
raw_comment: Wire bytes rather than decoded objects, for the rules decoding destroys: a number's spelling, a repeated key, and an unpaired surrogate. Each entry is the pristine signed envelope with one byte-level alteration, so the signature still covers the document a re-canonicalising verifier would reconstruct - a verifier that decodes and re-emits accepts every one of them. They MUST be fed through the entry point that takes bytes, which is the one a device uses; feeding them through a decoded-object entry point tests nothing, because the decode is the step under test.

cases.name: two_zone_site_correctly_bound
cases.note: Two clamps and two contactors, each pair bound by identity and proven by actuation. The two zones carry opposite commissioned mappings, so a verifier that derives one from a convention rather than reading it fails exactly one of them.

cases.name: local_gpio_control_path_proven_is_in_force
cases.note: The only shape that reaches in force: one local_gpio zone with both legs proven. The control leg records the level actually driven, which is what ties this pin at this polarity to this coil -- the thing the circuit leg cannot establish however carefully it was measured.

cases.name: control_path_undemonstrated_is_provisional
cases.note: Saying the control leg was not proven is accepted and is not authority. The document is retained provisionally, and the coil is never commanded on the polarity it asserts.

cases.name: control_leg_proven_over_an_undemonstrated_circuit_leg_is_provisional
cases.note: The pin is known to move the coil and nothing is known about which circuit that coil switches. Commanding it would open an unidentified circuit -- the transposition hazard this contract exists for, reached by a route that looks well proven. Neither leg substitutes for the other, so this is provisional however good the control proof is.

proof.reason: load could not be interrupted at commissioning

cases.name: a_provisional_record_does_not_advance_the_chain
cases.note: A provisional binding was already held at binding_seq 1 and nothing was ever in force, so the freshness floor is still 0 and this document at seq 1 is accepted. Entering provisional records into the succession would strand the chain behind a document that never carried authority.

cases.name: pre_energisation_proof_accepted
cases.note: Terminal states proven at the terminals with a meter before the site load was first energised. Acceptable for autonomous actuation: the association is measured, not asserted.

cases.name: undemonstrated_zone_accepted_in_development
cases.note: Document is well-formed and accepted. The borehole zone's actuating profiles stay inactive and the runtime logs a consolidated WARNING; its non-actuating profiles remain available. The main zone is unaffected.

binding.reason: load could not be interrupted at commissioning

proof.reason: borehole pump serves a live ward; interruption refused by site

cases.name: revision_with_fresh_proof_accepted
cases.note: A recalibration changes `calibration_ref`, so the prior proof no longer establishes the binding and a fresh one is carried. `supersedes` names the canonical hash of the document it replaces.

cases.name: polarity_revision_with_both_legs_fresh_is_in_force
cases.note: A driver board that inverts the stage changes `active_high`, so neither leg of the old proof survives it: the circuit leg is redone and the control leg is redone against the new polarity. Both are performed after the retained document, so the revision reaches in force.

binding.reason: driver board replaced; the stage inverts

cases.name: capacity_only_revision_keeps_its_proof
cases.note: The revision changes `rated_capacity` and carries both proof legs, each exactly as old as the retained record. Capacity is the one zone field a proof does not establish, so the revision reaches in force after its bounds are checked again. The retained state holds no capacity, so a consumer cannot tell this case from an unchanged revision; what it pins is that a carried proof on a zone whose sensor, actuator and mapping are unchanged is accepted.

binding.reason: breaker upgraded from 10 A to 16 A

cases.name: revision_after_a_record_with_no_control_leg
cases.note: The retained record carried no control leg, so there is no control time for a revision's control leg to follow. The revision rewires the mapping and carries a fresh circuit leg and a control leg; with nothing retained to inherit, the control leg is fresh by construction and the zone reaches in force.

binding.reason: contactor rewired and both legs proven

cases.name: zone_renamed_on_the_same_hardware_keeps_its_proof
cases.note: The revision renames the zone and changes nothing else. A zone's name labels it; the proof established the sensor, the actuator and the mapping, and none of those moved, so the carried legs stand and the zone reaches in force.

cases.name: another_channel_on_the_same_board_is_not_its_predecessor
cases.note: The same board on another channel is a different actuator. Nothing retained shares its name, its sensor or its identity, so there is no proof for it to inherit; it is verified as a new zone, provisional as every firmware zone is. A consumer that matched firmware actuators on the board alone would refuse it.

binding.reason: pump moved to the board's second relay; clamp moved to the tank

cases.name: an_unclaimed_leg_is_not_held_to_the_retained_proof
cases.note: The mapping is rewired and the circuit leg is recorded undemonstrated, with the time of the retained proof. A leg the revision does not claim carries no proof, so it is not held to the retained time: the zone is provisional, never in force, and never refused as stale.

cases.name: an_unclaimed_control_leg_is_not_held_to_the_retained_proof
cases.note: The mapping is rewired and the circuit leg redone; the control leg is recorded undemonstrated with the time of the retained proof. A leg the revision does not claim is held to no time, so the zone is provisional and not refused as stale.

binding.reason: contactor rewired; circuit re-proven, control leg to follow

cases.name: control_leg_dropped_on_a_changed_zone_is_provisional
cases.note: The mapping is rewired, the circuit leg redone and the control leg left out. The retained record has a control time, but an absent leg carries no proof and is held to none, so the zone is provisional and not refused as stale.

binding.reason: contactor rewired; circuit re-proven, control leg dropped

cases.name: circuit_leg_between_the_two_retained_times_is_fresh
cases.note: The circuit leg follows the retained circuit proof and precedes the retained control proof; the control leg follows the retained control proof. Each leg is held to the retained time of the same leg, so both are fresh; a consumer that held both to the later of the two retained times refuses it.

binding.reason: contactor rewired and both legs proven

cases.name: name_taken_by_unchanged_hardware_fresh_against_that_zone
cases.note: The main circuit's hardware, unchanged, takes the name of the retained `feeder` zone with legs fresh against `feeder`. Against its own retained zone nothing changed, so it is not held to that zone's later proof; a consumer that, once any match changed, held the zone to every match refuses it. Its legs predate its own zone's retained proof, so this case depends on whether an unchanged zone may carry an older proof, which the contract leaves open.

binding.reason: main circuit renamed to feeder and re-proven

cases.name: proof_only_revision_carries_its_control_leg
cases.note: Nothing in the zone changes; the circuit leg is re-proven and the control leg carried. A new proof time is not a change to the zone, so the carried control leg stands and the zone reaches in force.

cases.name: control_leg_between_the_two_retained_times_is_fresh
cases.note: The retained control proof predates the retained circuit proof, and the new control leg falls between them. Each leg is held to the retained time of the same leg, so the control leg is fresh and the revision reaches in force; a consumer that held it to the later of the two retained times refuses it.

binding.reason: contactor rewired and both legs proven

cases.name: firmware_zone_on_another_board_is_not_its_predecessor
cases.note: The same channel name on a different board is a different actuator. Nothing retained shares its name, its sensor or its identity, so there is no proof for it to inherit and no revision rule to apply; it is verified as a new zone, provisional as every firmware zone is. A consumer that matched on the channel alone would refuse it.

binding.reason: pump zone renamed; clamp moved to the tank input

reject_cases.name: transposed_binding
reject_cases.note: The contact was observed to open and the instrument still finds the load energised afterwards, because the clamp is on a different circuit from the contactor. This is the transposition case, and it is caught by the instrument's own load determination rather than by reading a threshold into a current value.

reject_cases.name: terminal_state_observed_contradicts_command
reject_cases.note: The contact was observed closed after a command to open the circuit.

reject_cases.name: proof_performed_on_an_idle_load
reject_cases.note: The load was not drawing before the open command, so opening it demonstrated nothing: an idle circuit reads the same on both sides of an actuation. A low reading after the command is not on its own evidence that this contactor controls this circuit.

reject_cases.name: proof_delta_within_the_sensor_noise_floor
reject_cases.note: The instrument reports the load gone, and the recorded current moved by 0.02 A against a declared noise floor of 0.05 A. A change the sensor cannot resolve is not a measurement, whatever the instrument says.

reject_cases.name: proof_open_observed_without_the_load_it_interrupted
reject_cases.note: The recorded current falls well past the noise floor, and the instrument reports no load present on either side of the open command. Only the instrument's classification contradicts the command here, so a verifier that reads the sensor values and skips the booleans accepts it. The readings are evidence; the instrument decides.

reject_cases.name: proof_close_observed_with_no_readings_and_the_load_already_present
reject_cases.note: A close command on a circuit the instrument already reports energised establishes nothing, and this observation carries no readings at all, so the noise-floor rule cannot reach it. Without the classifier there is no rule left to refuse it.

reject_cases.name: polarity_mismatch
reject_cases.note: `active_high` is false, so a de-energised coil is driven by a high GPIO level. The observation records a low level for the de-energised command, which contradicts the declared driver polarity.

reject_cases.name: outcomes_name_one_coil_state
reject_cases.note: Both circuit outcomes map to `de_energised`. A coil has two states, so one of the two observations is wrong.

reject_cases.name: terminal_state_contradicts_open_outcome
reject_cases.note: `open_protected_circuit` is `de_energised` while `de_energised_terminal_state` is `closed`. Both cannot be observations of the same channel.

reject_cases.name: capacity_above_sensor_full_scale
reject_cases.note: A 120 A capacity on a clamp that reads to 100 A describes a load the sensor cannot measure at all.

reject_cases.name: trip_point_above_sensor_full_scale
reject_cases.note: Capacity is comfortably in range at 25 A, and the release-owned multiplier of 5.0 puts the trip point at 125 A, beyond the clamp's 100 A full scale. A saturating sensor reports the hazard as a merely high reading, so the cutoff can never fire. This is the case a capacity-only bound misses.

reject_cases.name: signed_by_provisioning_authority
reject_cases.note: Genuinely signed by the provisioning authority, which is why the verdict is reachable at all: it is decided after the signature verifies, so a stranger cannot manufacture the event by naming that key over a forged signature. Refused because the commercial plane must not be able to move a trip point by raising a declared capacity.

reject_cases.name: signed_by_previous_commissioning_generation
reject_cases.note: The previous generation is verify-only for the binding already in force. A new binding must be signed by the current generation, or a compromised key would keep authoring bindings after rotation.

reject_cases.name: signing_key_is_not_a_commissioning_generation
reject_cases.note: Self-consistent - the document names the key that signed it - and that key is neither generation of the commissioning anchor.

reject_cases.name: anchors_are_identical_key_material
reject_cases.note: Both configured anchors are the same 32 bytes, so `wrong_authority` could never be reached and the separation the contract rests on does not exist. Refused at configuration load, before any document is verified.

reject_cases.name: replayed_binding_seq
reject_cases.note: `binding_seq` does not strictly exceed the accepted one.

reject_cases.name: supersedes_does_not_match_accepted
reject_cases.note: `binding_seq` advances but `supersedes` names a document that is not the one in force, so the chain does not connect.

reject_cases.name: polarity_revised_without_a_fresh_control_proof
reject_cases.note: The revision inverts the driver stage and redoes the circuit leg, but carries the control proof performed against the old polarity. That proof recorded which level drove which coil state on the previous stage; under the new one it asserts the opposite. Accepting it would bring the zone into force with the polarity established by a measurement taken on the wiring it replaced -- the unproven-polarity actuation the control leg exists to close, reached through a revision rather than a first commissioning. The circuit leg is fresh, so the verdict is decided by the control leg alone.

binding.reason: driver board replaced; the stage inverts

reject_cases.name: sensor_rebound_without_fresh_proof
reject_cases.note: The revision binds the zone to a different declared clamp and carries both proof legs unchanged. Actuator identity, mapping and `calibration_ref` are exactly as retained, so the verdict is decided by the sensor alone. A proof records that this sensor observes this circuit; carried onto another sensor it asserts an association nobody observed, which is the transposition a proof exists to catch, reached through a revision rather than a first commissioning.

binding.reason: clamp moved to the feeder input

reject_cases.name: zone_renamed_without_fresh_proof
reject_cases.note: The revision inverts the driver stage and gives the zone a new name, carrying both proof legs from the retained record. Renaming a zone does not make its actuator new: the revision is compared against every retained zone sharing its zone id, its actuator identity or its sensor, and the retained zone on this pin was proven at the other polarity. Matching on the name alone would let a rename carry an unproven polarity into force.

reject_cases.name: zone_renamed_keeping_only_its_pin
reject_cases.note: The revision renames the zone, binds it to a different clamp and inverts the driver stage, keeping only the pin, and carries both proof legs. Its name, its sensor and its identity as a whole match no retained zone; only its pin does, so only a consumer that compares a GPIO actuator by its pin refuses it. The retained proof observed the old clamp at the other polarity.

binding.reason: zone renamed; clamp moved to the feeder input; stage inverts

reject_cases.name: zone_moved_keeping_only_its_name
reject_cases.note: The revision keeps the zone's name and moves it to another pin and another clamp, carrying both proof legs. Its actuator and its sensor match no retained zone; only its name does, so only a consumer that finds the retained zone by its name refuses it. The retained proof was taken on hardware this zone no longer uses.

binding.reason: contactor moved to pin 19; clamp moved to the feeder input

reject_cases.name: mapping_rewired_without_fresh_proof
reject_cases.note: The revision keeps the zone's name, pin, polarity and clamp, and records the contactor rewired so that the energised coil now opens the circuit, carrying both proof legs. Only the mapping changed, so the verdict is decided by it alone. The retained proof established the opposite mapping; carried onto this one it asserts the outcome a trip would command without anyone having observed it.

binding.reason: contactor rewired to its other contact

reject_cases.name: zone_held_to_every_retained_zone_it_matches
reject_cases.note: The revision keeps the zone's name, moves it to pin 13 and takes the clamp of another retained zone. It matches three retained zones: its own by name, the feeder by sensor, and the zone on pin 13 by pin. Its fresh legs follow its own zone's proof and pin 13's, but not the feeder's, which was proven later. A consumer that checks only the first match, the last, or stops at the first that passes accepts it; the rule holds the zone to every match, and the feeder's proof refuses it.

binding.reason: contactor moved to pin 13; clamp taken from the feeder zone

reject_cases.name: mapping_rewired_carrying_its_control_leg
reject_cases.note: The mapping is rewired and the circuit leg is redone, but the control leg is carried from the retained record. The control leg recorded which level drove which coil state under the old mapping; any change needs both legs refreshed, not only a change to the actuator, so the verdict is decided by the control leg alone.

binding.reason: contactor rewired; circuit re-proven, control leg carried

reject_cases.name: firmware_board_replaced_without_fresh_proof
reject_cases.note: The firmware zone keeps its name and clamp and moves to a new board on the same channel, carrying its proof. A firmware actuator is its board and its channel together, so the identity changed and the proof taken on the old board does not carry.

reject_cases.name: zone_found_by_sensor_id_not_by_the_whole_sensor
reject_cases.note: The revision renames the zone, moves it to pin 19 and recalibrates the clamp, carrying both proof legs. Only the `sensor_id` links it to the retained zone; the sensor as a whole differs. A consumer that finds a retained zone by the whole sensor finds nothing and accepts it.

binding.reason: zone renamed onto pin 19; clamp recalibrated

reject_cases.name: circuit_leg_carried_behind_a_fresh_control_leg
reject_cases.note: The mapping is rewired and the control leg redone, but the circuit leg is carried. A fresh control leg says the pin still moves the coil; it says nothing about what the coil now does to the circuit, so the carried circuit leg decides the case alone.

binding.reason: contactor rewired; control leg redone, circuit leg carried

reject_cases.name: sensor_changed_carrying_its_control_leg
reject_cases.note: Only the sensor changes, by its noise floor, and the circuit leg is redone, but the control leg is carried. Freshness is required of every claimed leg whichever field changed, so the control leg decides it; a consumer that refreshed the control leg only for an actuator or mapping change, or that noticed only a new sensor_id or calibration, accepts it.

binding.reason: clamp noise floor re-measured; circuit re-proven

reject_cases.name: control_leg_carried_behind_an_unclaimed_circuit_leg
reject_cases.note: The circuit leg is left undemonstrated, which holds it to no time, but the control leg is claimed and carried from the retained record. An unclaimed circuit leg does not excuse a claimed control leg, which is held to its retained time and refuses the case.

binding.reason: contactor rewired; circuit not yet proven, control leg carried

reject_cases.name: firmware_channel_moved_without_fresh_proof
reject_cases.note: The firmware zone keeps its name, clamp and board and moves to the board's other channel, carrying its proof. A firmware actuator is its board and its channel together, so the identity changed and the proof taken on the old channel does not carry.

binding.reason: pump moved to the board's second relay

reject_cases.name: name_taken_from_a_retained_zone
reject_cases.note: The revision keeps the main circuit's hardware exactly and renames it to `feeder`, the name of another retained zone proven on pin 19. Against its own hardware nothing changed; against `feeder`, whose name it takes, everything did, and its circuit leg is no later than `feeder`'s proof. A rename onto a retained zone's name is held to that zone. A consumer that stopped at the unchanged match, preferred the hardware match, looked only at the latest proof, or checked the circuit leg only on a single match accepts it.

binding.reason: main circuit renamed to feeder; the old feeder zone is retired

reject_cases.name: recalibrated_without_fresh_proof
reject_cases.note: The revision changes only the sensor's `calibration_ref`, a new calibration, and carries both proof legs. Every sensor field is part of what the proof established, so a consumer that compared the sensor without `calibration_ref` accepts a proof taken on a sensor described otherwise.

reject_cases.name: sensor_range_redeclared_without_fresh_proof
reject_cases.note: The revision changes only the sensor's `range_max`, a new upper range, and carries both proof legs. Every sensor field is part of what the proof established, so a consumer that compared the sensor without `range_max` accepts a proof taken on a sensor described otherwise.

reject_cases.name: sensor_lower_range_redeclared_without_fresh_proof
reject_cases.note: The revision changes only the sensor's `range_min`, a new lower range, and carries both proof legs. Every sensor field is part of what the proof established, so a consumer that compared the sensor without `range_min` accepts a proof taken on a sensor described otherwise.

reject_cases.name: sensor_unit_redeclared_without_fresh_proof
reject_cases.note: The revision changes only the sensor's `unit`, a new unit, and carries both proof legs. Every sensor field is part of what the proof established, so a consumer that compared the sensor without `unit` accepts a proof taken on a sensor described otherwise.

reject_cases.name: sensor_direction_flipped_without_fresh_proof
reject_cases.note: The revision changes only the sensor's `direction`, a reversed clamp, and carries both proof legs. Every sensor field is part of what the proof established, so a consumer that compared the sensor without `direction` accepts a proof taken on a sensor described otherwise.

reject_cases.name: sensor_quantity_redeclared_without_fresh_proof
reject_cases.note: The revision changes only the sensor's `quantity`, a new quantity, and carries both proof legs. Every sensor field is part of what the proof established, so a consumer that compared the sensor without `quantity` accepts a proof taken on a sensor described otherwise.

reject_cases.name: retained_zone_held_by_every_revision_zone_matching_it
reject_cases.note: Two revision zones match the one retained zone: the first takes its name on a new pin with fresh legs, the second keeps its pin and clamp under a new name, inverts the polarity and carries the proof. Each revision zone is held to every retained zone it matches, so the second is refused; a consumer that let each retained zone match only one revision zone gives it to the first and accepts the carried proof.

binding.reason: main moved to pin 19; its old contactor reused as a new zone

reject_cases.name: control_leg_stale_against_one_of_several_matches
reject_cases.note: The zone is matched by two retained zones, one by its pin and one by its name. Its circuit leg is fresh against both and its control leg is fresh against the second but no later than the first's control proof. A consumer that checked the control leg only when a single retained zone matched accepts it.

binding.reason: renamed to feeder on pin 26 with a spare clamp

reject_cases.name: circuit_leg_carried_behind_an_undemonstrated_control_leg
reject_cases.note: The mapping is rewired, the control leg is left undemonstrated and the circuit leg is carried. An unclaimed control leg does not excuse a claimed circuit leg, which is held to its retained time and refuses the case.

binding.reason: contactor rewired; circuit carried, control leg to follow

reject_cases.name: pre_energisation_leg_carried_without_fresh_proof
reject_cases.note: The clamp is recalibrated and the control leg redone, but the circuit leg is a pre_energisation proof carried from the retained record. A meter proof is a claimed leg like an actuation proof, held to the retained time; a consumer that counted only actuate_and_observe as claimed exempts it.

binding.reason: clamp recalibrated; control leg redone, meter proof carried

reject_cases.name: circuit_leg_held_to_its_own_retained_time_not_the_earlier
reject_cases.note: The retained control proof predates the retained circuit proof. Both new legs fall between them: the control leg is fresh, the circuit leg is not. Each leg is held to the retained time of the same leg, so the circuit leg refuses it; a consumer that held the circuit leg to the earlier of the two retained times accepts it.

binding.reason: contactor rewired and both legs proven

reject_cases.name: active_high_changed_with_only_the_circuit_leg_carried
reject_cases.note: Only `active_high` changes. The other leg is redone and the circuit leg is carried from the retained record. A change to any field requires every claimed leg to be fresh, not the leg a reader might pair with `active_high`; a consumer that exempted the circuit leg for this change accepts it.

binding.reason: active_high changed; the circuit leg carried

binding.reason: quantity changed; the circuit leg carried

A change to any field requires every claimed leg to be fresh, not the leg a reader might pair with `calibration_ref`; a consumer that exempted the control leg for this change accepts it.

binding.reason: calibration_ref changed; the control leg carried

reject_cases.name: sensor_replaced_with_only_the_circuit_leg_carried
reject_cases.note: Only `sensor_id`, `calibration_ref` change, together: a replaced clamp. The other leg is redone and the circuit leg is carried. A consumer that exempted the circuit leg for a replaced clamp accepts it.

binding.reason: 2 fields changed; the circuit leg carried

reject_cases.name: actuator_replaced_with_only_the_circuit_leg_carried
reject_cases.note: Only `gpio_pin`, `active_high` change, together: a replaced driver. The other leg is redone and the circuit leg is carried. A consumer that exempted the circuit leg for a replaced driver accepts it.

binding.reason: 2 fields changed; the circuit leg carried

reject_cases.name: rewired_to_another_pin_with_only_the_circuit_leg_carried
reject_cases.note: Only `gpio_pin`, `mapping` change, together: a rewired actuator. The other leg is redone and the circuit leg is carried. A consumer that exempted the circuit leg for a rewired actuator accepts it.

binding.reason: 2 fields changed; the circuit leg carried

reject_cases.name: polarity_flipped_with_its_mapping_with_only_the_circuit_leg_carried
reject_cases.note: Only `active_high`, `mapping` change, together: a polarity flip whose mapping flips with it. The other leg is redone and the circuit leg is carried. A consumer that exempted the circuit leg for a polarity flip whose mapping flips with it accepts it.

binding.reason: 2 fields changed; the circuit leg carried

reject_cases.name: every_field_changed_with_only_the_circuit_leg_carried
reject_cases.note: The sensor and the actuator are both redeclared in every field. The other leg is redone and the circuit leg is carried. A consumer that exempted the circuit leg once enough fields changed, reading the zone as new rather than revised, accepts it.

binding.reason: 11 fields changed; the circuit leg carried

reject_cases.name: sensor_replaced_with_only_the_control_leg_carried
reject_cases.note: Only `sensor_id`, `calibration_ref` change, together: a replaced clamp. The other leg is redone and the control leg is carried. A consumer that exempted the control leg for a replaced clamp accepts it.

binding.reason: 2 fields changed; the control leg carried

reject_cases.name: actuator_replaced_with_only_the_control_leg_carried
reject_cases.note: Only `gpio_pin`, `active_high` change, together: a replaced driver. The other leg is redone and the control leg is carried. A consumer that exempted the control leg for a replaced driver accepts it.

binding.reason: 2 fields changed; the control leg carried

reject_cases.name: rewired_to_another_pin_with_only_the_control_leg_carried
reject_cases.note: Only `gpio_pin`, `mapping` change, together: a rewired actuator. The other leg is redone and the control leg is carried. A consumer that exempted the control leg for a rewired actuator accepts it.

binding.reason: 2 fields changed; the control leg carried

reject_cases.name: polarity_flipped_with_its_mapping_with_only_the_control_leg_carried
reject_cases.note: Only `active_high`, `mapping` change, together: a polarity flip whose mapping flips with it. The other leg is redone and the control leg is carried. A consumer that exempted the control leg for a polarity flip whose mapping flips with it accepts it.

binding.reason: 2 fields changed; the control leg carried

reject_cases.name: every_field_changed_with_only_the_control_leg_carried
reject_cases.note: The sensor and the actuator are both redeclared in every field. The other leg is redone and the control leg is carried. A consumer that exempted the control leg once enough fields changed, reading the zone as new rather than revised, accepts it.

binding.reason: 11 fields changed; the control leg carried

reject_cases.name: actuator_kind_changed_carrying_the_circuit_leg
reject_cases.note: The pump zone moves from a firmware relay channel to a local pin, keeping its name, clamp and mapping, and carries its circuit leg. The retained zone had no control leg, so the circuit leg decides it alone. A consumer that compared identities only within one actuator kind, and so saw no change, accepts it.

binding.reason: pump moved from the relay board to a local pin

reject_cases.name: control_leg_carried_behind_a_fresh_pre_energisation_leg
reject_cases.note: The clamp is recalibrated and the circuit leg redone as a pre_energisation meter proof, but the control leg is carried. A meter proof never drives the pin, so it cannot stand in for the control leg; a consumer that exempted the control leg behind one accepts it.

binding.reason: clamp recalibrated; meter proof redone, control leg carried

reject_cases.name: circuit_leg_carried_in_development_posture
reject_cases.note: The mapping is rewired, the control leg redone and the circuit leg carried, in development posture. Posture decides what a provisional zone may do, not whether a carried proof is fresh; a consumer that held the circuit leg to its retained time only in production accepts it.

binding.reason: contactor rewired; control leg redone, circuit leg carried

reject_cases.name: circuit_leg_carried_in_staging_posture
reject_cases.note: The mapping is rewired, the other leg redone and the circuit leg carried, in staging posture. Posture never decides whether a carried proof is fresh; a consumer that held the leg to its retained time only in production accepts it.

binding.reason: 1 fields changed; the circuit leg carried

reject_cases.name: control_leg_carried_in_staging_posture
reject_cases.note: The mapping is rewired, the other leg redone and the control leg carried, in staging posture. Posture never decides whether a carried proof is fresh; a consumer that held the leg to its retained time only in production accepts it.

binding.reason: 1 fields changed; the control leg carried

reject_cases.name: actuator_kind_changed_to_firmware_carrying_the_circuit_leg
reject_cases.note: A zone in force on a local pin moves to a firmware relay channel, keeping its name, clamp and mapping, and carries its circuit leg; a firmware zone claims no control leg. A consumer that compared identities only within one actuator kind, and so saw no change, accepts it.

binding.reason: main contactor moved from the local pin to a relay board

reject_cases.name: zone_found_by_its_sensor_id_alone
reject_cases.note: The revision renames the zone, moves it to another pin and redeclares every sensor field but `sensor_id`, carrying both legs. Only the sensor_id finds the retained zone, so a consumer that matched a sensor by its id together with any other field finds nothing.

binding.reason: zone renamed; contactor moved to pin 19; clamp re-declared

reject_cases.name: zone_renamed_keeping_only_its_sensor
reject_cases.note: The revision renames the zone and moves it to another pin, keeping only the clamp, and carries both proof legs. Its name and its actuator match no retained zone; only its sensor does, so only a consumer that finds the retained zone by the sensor refuses it. The retained proof was taken on the old contactor.

binding.reason: zone renamed; contactor moved to pin 19

reject_cases.name: firmware_zone_renamed_keeping_only_its_channel
reject_cases.note: The revision renames the firmware zone and binds it to a different clamp, keeping the same board and channel, and carries its proof. Only the actuator identity matches a retained zone, and a firmware actuator is identified by its board and its channel together, so the retained zone is found and the carried proof is refused.

binding.reason: pump zone renamed; clamp moved to the tank input

reject_cases.name: actuator_replaced_without_fresh_proof
reject_cases.note: The revision moves the main contactor to a different GPIO pin and carries the previous proof unchanged. A new actuator does not inherit the mapping the previous one was proven to have. The declared hardware changed, so `inventory_generation` advances to 8: reusing 7 for a different set of actuators is exactly what the non-reuse rule forbids, and a corpus that did so would contradict the contract it certifies. Advancing it changes nothing about the verdict - the proof is stale either way - which is the point: a correct generation does not rescue an actuator that was never demonstrated.

reject_cases.name: undemonstrated_zone_under_hardened_posture
reject_cases.note: Same document as the accepted development case. Under production posture an undemonstrated zone cannot activate an actuating profile, and a runtime that quietly disabled the cutoff while reporting healthy is the worst available outcome, so startup fails.

binding.reason: load could not be interrupted at commissioning

proof.reason: borehole pump serves a live ward; interruption refused by site

reject_cases.name: duplicate_actuator_identity
reject_cases.note: Two zones claim the same contactor. Refused rather than resolved: there is no ordering preference and no nearest-match rule.

reject_cases.name: duplicate_sensor_id
reject_cases.note: One clamp bound into two zones with different actuators.

reject_cases.name: sensor_absent_from_declared_inventory
reject_cases.note: A binding may only name hardware the device declared.

reject_cases.name: declared_actuator_left_unbound
reject_cases.note: The device declares two actuators and the document binds one. Refused in hardened posture rather than silently leaving a contactor ungoverned.

reject_cases.name: wrong_device
reject_cases.note: A binding signed for one device must never be accepted by another.

reject_cases.name: bad_signature
reject_cases.note: Names the current commissioning key and is signed by someone who does not hold it. Key selection finds the named key and the signature is what refuses; no authority verdict is issued over an unverified document.

reject_cases.name: unknown_actuator_kind
reject_cases.note: `kind` is a closed vocabulary. An unrecognised kind is refused, never treated as the nearest known one.

reject_cases.name: reason_absent
reject_cases.note: `actor` and `reason` are structurally required, so a document missing either is a shape violation rejected before signature verification. There is no audit-specific verdict.

reject_cases.name: mapping_key_absent
reject_cases.note: The mapping has no default: a channel missing any of its three facts cannot be actuated.

reject_cases.name: signing_key_with_non_canonical_padding
reject_cases.note: A different spelling of the same 32 bytes: strict base64 accepts it and it decodes to the identical key. Only round-trip equality refuses it, and without that rule two implementations disagree about a document neither considers malformed.

reject_cases.name: signing_key_is_not_valid_base64
reject_cases.note: The signed body names a key that is not base64 at all. A verifier that raises here rather than returning a verdict has not refused the document.

reject_cases.name: signing_key_is_not_thirty_two_bytes
reject_cases.note: Well-formed base64 that is not an Ed25519 public key. Length is part of the grammar, so this never reaches key selection.

reject_cases.name: inventory_generation_absent
reject_cases.note: Required, with no default. A binding that does not say which inventory it was commissioned against cannot be shown to describe the hardware the device currently declares.

reject_cases.name: inventory_generation_is_zero
reject_cases.note: A binding is commissioned against an inventory, so there must be one to name. No device/site contract defines generation zero as a signed inventory, which makes zero a binding to absence rather than an early state.

reject_cases.name: inventory_generation_is_negative
reject_cases.note: Below the floor by a different route than zero, and the case a verifier clamping instead of refusing would silently admit.

reject_cases.name: inventory_generation_is_a_float
reject_cases.note: Canonical bytes separate 7 from 7.0, and language runtimes disagree about whether the second is integer-like: Go unmarshals both into float64, and Python's 7.0 == 7 is true. A verifier deciding on numeric equality accepts a spelling the contract does not define.

reject_cases.name: capacity_spelled_as_an_integer
reject_cases.note: A capacity is a `number`, and this contract fixes a number's spelling by the field's declared type rather than by its value: 10.0 and 10 are different signing inputs for one capacity, and nothing in the value says which the schema meant. Both verifiers accepted this before the rule was written, so the corpus could not see the divergence it allowed.

reject_cases.name: v_is_a_boolean
reject_cases.note: In Python True == 1, so a version check written as an inequality against 1 admits a boolean. The canonical bytes then carry `true` where every other consumer expects `1`.

reject_cases.name: v_is_a_float
reject_cases.note: The version is an integer, and 1.0 is not 1 on the wire however the two compare in a given language.

reject_cases.name: inventory_generation_is_a_string
reject_cases.note: A quoted generation compares differently from an integer one, and the comparison is what ties a binding to an inventory.

reject_cases.name: inventory_generation_is_a_boolean
reject_cases.note: JSON separates booleans from numbers and some languages do not: in Python True is an instance of int, so a naive check reads this as generation 1.

reject_cases.name: control_path_without_a_gpio_level
reject_cases.note: The level driven is the whole evidence of this leg. Without it the observation records that a command was issued and says nothing about which pin state accompanied it, which is what the circuit leg already failed to establish.

reject_cases.name: control_path_gpio_level_contradicts_the_polarity
reject_cases.note: active_high is false, so an energised coil is driven low. A leg claiming it was driven high has not proven this driver stage; it has recorded a document that disagrees with itself about the one fact it exists to settle.

reject_cases.name: one_sided_circuit_proof
reject_cases.note: The circuit leg observes only the closing outcome, so the direction it leaves undemonstrated is the one a cutoff exists for. Its control leg is complete, so the one-sided leg is what decides the verdict.

reject_cases.name: one_sided_control_path_proof
reject_cases.note: The control leg observes only the closing outcome while the circuit leg is complete. A consumer tallying outcomes once across both legs, rather than per leg, lets the circuit leg's observations complete this one and accepts the document to in force.

reject_cases.name: coil_state_contradicts_the_mapping
reject_cases.note: One circuit-leg observation records the coil in the state the mapping assigns to the other outcome. `gpio_level` agrees with the coil state recorded and every other fact agrees with the command, so the coil comparison alone decides it -- the join where the mapping and the evidence must agree.

reject_cases.name: control_path_coil_state_contradicts_the_mapping
reject_cases.note: The same contradiction in the control leg. A consumer enforcing the coil comparison for `proof` and omitting it for `proof.control_path` -- the shape a separate code path per leg produces -- refuses the three vectors above and accepts this one to in force.

reject_cases.name: control_path_carries_an_unknown_field
reject_cases.note: Closed like every other object here. A field a consumer silently drops turns a misspelt claim about the control path into one that appears to its author to have taken effect.

reject_cases.name: control_path_undemonstrated_carrying_observations
reject_cases.note: An unproven leg claiming observations is claiming a proof it also says it does not have.

reject_cases.name: firmware_channel_claiming_a_commanded_control_path
reject_cases.note: The method names an operation that exists for a pin and does not yet exist for a channel: firmware holds its mapping before it can actuate, so there is no designed way to command one through the path under test. Admitting it would bring a firmware zone into force on a proof no design defines, which is worse than having no method at all.

reject_cases.name: inventory_generation_altered_without_resigning
reject_cases.note: The field sits inside the signed body precisely so this fails. An intermediary raising the generation would let a stale binding claim currency over hardware it was never commissioned against. The signature here covers generation 7 and the document on the wire says 9.

reject_cases.name: supersedes_is_not_a_digest
reject_cases.note: `supersedes` is either null or a lowercase sha256 digest; a free string would make the revision chain unverifiable.

reject_cases.name: actuator_kind_is_an_array
reject_cases.note: A closed vocabulary tested by membership before its type is checked raises rather than refuses: arrays and objects are unhashable. Every vocabulary in this contract has the same shape, so one of them is carried as the representative case.

reject_cases.name: proof_method_is_an_object
reject_cases.note: The same defect on a different vocabulary, and on the field that selects which shape the rest of the proof must have.

reject_cases.name: noise_floor_declared_as_a_boolean
reject_cases.note: JSON separates booleans from numbers and some languages do not: in Python True is an instance of int, so a naive numeric check accepts this. A verifier that does is reading a threshold out of a flag.

reject_cases.name: signer_id_is_whitespace_only
reject_cases.note: A field carrying no information is not a field that was supplied, and an empty signer in an audit record is worse than an absent one because it looks answered.

reject_cases.name: unknown_sensor_field
reject_cases.note: The closed grammar reaches nested objects. A sensor field a consumer does not read is refused rather than dropped.

reject_cases.name: unknown_observation_field
reject_cases.note: An observation is a closed shape too. An extra field in a proof is a claim about how the proof was performed, and an ignored claim is worse than a refused one.

reject_cases.name: identity_shape_does_not_match_actuator_kind
reject_cases.note: A local-GPIO identity on a firmware channel names an actuator that does not exist, and would leave active_high unread on a device with no pin.

reject_cases.name: gpio_level_recorded_for_a_firmware_channel
reject_cases.note: A pin level is meaningless for a channel with no pin, so recording one is a shape error rather than an ignorable extra.

reject_cases.name: one_sided_sensor_reading
reject_cases.note: Readings are paired: a before with no after cannot show a change, and a verifier that skipped the delta rule on a missing field would silently accept the weaker proof.

reject_cases.name: superseded_derivation_field_present
reject_cases.note: `contact_type` is the field this contract exists to make unrepresentable. Unknown keys inside a zone are refused so a stale safety field cannot be silently ignored by a consumer that does not read it.

envelope_reject_cases.name: envelope_carries_an_unknown_field
envelope_reject_cases.note: A field beside the signature is outside the signed bytes, so it is unauthenticated by construction. Ignoring it lets an intermediary add content a careless consumer might read.

envelope_reject_cases.name: envelope_signature_absent
envelope_reject_cases.note: An unsigned document is not a weakly signed one.

envelope_reject_cases.name: envelope_signature_without_its_algorithm_prefix
envelope_reject_cases.note: The wire encoding is `ed25519:<base64>`; a bare base64 string does not say what algorithm produced it.

envelope_reject_cases.name: envelope_signature_is_not_valid_base64
envelope_reject_cases.note: Refused by the grammar rather than by a decoder throwing inside verification.

envelope_reject_cases.name: envelope_signature_is_the_wrong_length
envelope_reject_cases.note: Ed25519 signatures are 64 bytes. A value that was never a candidate authenticator is malformed rather than a failed authentication.

envelope_reject_cases.name: envelope_signature_with_non_canonical_padding
envelope_reject_cases.note: The same 64 bytes spelled differently. The rule that applies to a public key applies to a signature for the same reason.

envelope_reject_cases.name: envelope_binding_is_not_an_object
envelope_reject_cases.note: The wrapper names one document; a string is not one.

envelope_reject_cases.name: profile_envelope_carries_an_unknown_field
envelope_reject_cases.note: The same rule as the binding envelope, on the shape a firmware device actually receives. A field outside the signed bytes is unauthenticated by construction whichever document it accompanies.

envelope_reject_cases.name: profile_envelope_signature_is_not_valid_base64
envelope_reject_cases.note: Refused by the grammar rather than by a decoder throwing inside verification, on the constrained consumer where that distinction matters most.

envelope_reject_cases.name: profile_envelope_signature_with_non_canonical_padding
envelope_reject_cases.note: The same 64 bytes spelled differently, in the profile envelope.

envelope_reject_cases.name: profile_envelope_signature_absent
envelope_reject_cases.note: An unsigned profile is not a weakly signed one.

raw_reject_cases.name: capacity_in_exponent_notation
raw_reject_cases.note: The same capacity, spelled the one way the agreement zone excludes. Decode it and re-emit and the signature verifies, so a verifier that re-canonicalises before comparing accepts a document a byte-comparing consumer refuses. Exponent notation never appears on the wire.

raw_reject_cases.name: capacity_with_a_trailing_zero
raw_reject_cases.note: 10.00 and 10.0 are the same number and different bytes. The shortest round-tripping form is the only one this contract defines, for the reason strict base64 was not enough for a key: more than one spelling means more than one signing input for one value.

raw_reject_cases.name: timestamp_spelled_with_a_negative_zero
raw_reject_cases.note: The other half of the spelling rule, on an integer field. -0 and 0 are one value and two signing inputs, and no check on the decoded number can see the difference: both arrive as 0. Only the shortest-form rule reaches it.

raw_reject_cases.name: duplicate_key_in_the_binding
raw_reject_cases.note: A last-wins parser reads binding_seq 1 and verifies the signature over it; a first-wins parser reads 5 from the same file. Which occurrence survives is a property of the parser, so the canonical form of the object is undefined and the bytes are refused rather than resolved.

raw_reject_cases.name: duplicate_key_with_equal_values
raw_reject_cases.note: The harmless-looking case, refused for the same reason: telling it from the dangerous one requires decoding both occurrences, which is the step the rule exists to make unnecessary.

raw_reject_cases.name: duplicate_signature_in_the_envelope
raw_reject_cases.note: The wrapper is closed, and closing it means the key set as written rather than the key set as decoded. A second signature beside the first is unauthenticated by construction whichever one a parser keeps.

raw_reject_cases.name: unpaired_surrogate_in_a_string
raw_reject_cases.note: The document is valid UTF-8 on disk and carries a lone surrogate only after decoding, where CPython raises on re-encoding and Go silently substitutes U+FFFD. Two verifiers then disagree about the bytes a signature covers over a document neither calls malformed, so it is refused before canonicalisation and before any signature is checked.

firmware_profile_cases.name: profile_matches_the_accepted_binding
firmware_profile_cases.note: The device holds the mapping itself, signed by the commissioning authority and bound to the binding hash. A runtime and a device that both verify this object cannot disagree about which coil state opens the circuit.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_mapping_disagrees_with_the_binding
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: Correct binding hash, inverted mapping. This is the case a manifest reference cannot catch: the hashes match and the device drives the opposite coil state. Only carrying the mapping inside the signed object makes it detectable.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_names_a_different_binding
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: The mapping is right for a document that is not the one in force. The sequence still parses, so the refusal is the binding check rather than the grammar.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_binding_hash_is_malformed
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: `binding_hash` is a lowercase sha256 digest. A free string would make the tie between a profile and the binding it came from unverifiable.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_signing_key_is_malformed
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: A key that is not 32 bytes of strict base64 is refused by the grammar, before any key can be selected.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_for_another_channel
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: A profile is scoped to one channel on one device.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_signed_by_the_provisioning_authority
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: Same authority rule as the binding, and decided the same way: after the signature verifies, so a build system cannot commission a channel by signing its own profile and cannot manufacture the verdict either.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_for_another_device
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: A profile signed for one firmware device must never actuate another, the same rule inbound commands already enforce.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_with_an_unknown_field
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: The profile is a closed shape. An unrecognised key is refused rather than ignored, so a stale mapping field cannot ride along unread.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_bad_signature
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: Names the current commissioning key and is signed by someone who does not hold it. Exercises the profile's own signature stage, which the binding corpus cannot cover on its behalf.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_signed_by_the_previous_commissioning_generation
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: Rotation applies to a profile exactly as it does to a binding: the previous generation verifies and does not sign. Reported as superseded rather than unknown, because dismissing it at key selection would describe our own rotated key as a stranger and hide that the profile was once legitimately signed.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_anchors_are_identical_key_material
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: A collision involving the previous generation is as fatal as one involving the current: if either commissioning anchor is the provisioning key, the separation the contract rests on does not exist for profiles either.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_signing_key_is_not_an_anchor
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: Self-consistent and signed by a key that is neither configured anchor, so no candidate can be selected and no signature is attempted.
